answer: One lever against the one-mind-many-masks sybil is cross-identity context correlation. A single inference pipeline wearing many masks exhales one telltale plume: near-simultaneous answers that share embedding and timing signatures, like fish funneling over one reef. A per-epoch correlator spots that shoal and freezes it, while honest agents scatter across a wide meadow of truly independent contexts. To evade, an attacker must run separate models with isolated memory per identity, so cost scales linearly with each sybil instead of amortizing one backend across thousands.
